import pandas as pd
import openpyxl

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paths
input_path = "/mnt/data/spreadsheet/53161/1_53161_input.xlsx"
output_path = "/mnt/data/outputs/53161_0_922fb5b8/1_53161_output.xlsx"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load workbook and sheet
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(input_path)
ws = wb["Sheet1"]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load data into DataFrame (no header) for easy slicing
df = pd.read_excel(input_path, sheet_name="Sheet1", header=None)

# Locate header row where column E (index 4) == "Agent"
header_row_idx = df[df.iloc[:, 4] == "Agent"].index[0]

# Determine last row with an agent name (non‑NaN in column E)
last_agent_row_idx = df.iloc[:, 4].last_valid_index()

# Category columns start at column F (index 5) and span 9 categories
cat_start = 5
cat_end = cat_start + 9  # exclusive

# Extract the numeric category matrix for all agents
cat_matrix = df.iloc[header_row_idx + 1 : last_agent_row_idx + 1,
                    cat_start : cat_end]

# Convert to numeric (treat non‑numeric as 0) and sum each column
cat_sums = pd.to_numeric(cat_matrix.stack(), errors='coerce').groupby(level=1).sum()
# Ensure we have exactly 9 sums (Category 1‑9)
cat_sums = [int(cat_sums.get(i, 0)) for i in range(9)]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare the block for F22:AE29 (8 rows × 26 columns)
# 9 category totals + 17 blanks = 26 columns
rows_to_write = []
for _ in range(8):  # rows 22‑29
    row = cat_sums + [""] * (26 - len(cat_sums))

# Write the block
start_row, start_col = 22, 6   # F = column 6
for r_offset, row_vals in enumerate(rows_to_write):
    for c_offset, val in enumerate(row_vals):
        ws.cell(row=start_row + r_offset, column=start_col + c_offset, value=val)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save the modified workbook
wb.save(output_path)
print(f"Written corrected block to {output_path}")
